structs.name: playlistInfo
structs.size_evidence: best value 928 (game-test and IDA 992 are not Replay). Strongest evidence: every playlist accessor indexes the same record array with 232 dwords per record, i.e. a 928-byte stride: Playlist_GetEntry@0x1410CC870 (imul rcx, rax, 3A0h), Playlist_GetOrdinalRowWord@0x1410CC560, Playlist_GetItemVideo@0x1410CCEB0, Playlist_UpdateXPScales@0x1410D3BD0, Playlist_RunRules@0x1410D23E0, and about 20 more; Playlist_CountPopulatedEntries@0x1410CD400 steps 1392 words (3 records of 928 bytes) per unrolled iteration. Blocker: the array lives inside the zoneList global (IDA-typed scrContext_t, so field names are wrong), so the element type is inferred from field semantics, and the absolute offsets are not fixed: Playlist_GetPlaylistNamePtr@0x1410CD4C0 returns record start + 0 at 4*37932 bytes = 864 bytes before the firstEntry word (LOWORD of 4*38148 in Playlist_GetEntry), which places firstEntry at 864 only if the name is at offset 0 (the name pointer can be at most 5 bytes into a record that ends at +922 for the last accessed byte). The record fits 928 bytes only if the name is at 0..5 and the accessors at 856/860 (RecordId, flags) sit inside the IDA video/context area, so the pre-firstEntry layout is not settled.
unconfirmed: record stride 928 = sizeof(playlistInfo) in Replay: strongly supported, element type not proven

structs.notes: Not resolved: the record is 928 bytes in Replay, not 992. The shift from game-test is 64 bytes (the difference is exactly the context / dc_restrict / rules / requiredDLCMask / flags block in game-test), and the numRounds / time_limit / score_limit accessors line up with game-test names at -64 (Playlist_GetAuxDword0C, 14, 18), which supports the 928-byte record with firstEntry at 864. The item accessors (Playlist_GetItemImage, GetItemVideo, GetItemCategoryClass) read other record areas and are not evidence for this layout. The IDA playlistInfo should not be changed until the coordinator decides on 928 vs 992 with the name-offset window (name at 0..5 inside the record).
